title: CVE-2026-98432: Critical Linux Kernel TCP Flaw Enables Remote Code Execution
content_md: A critical vulnerability in the Linux kernel’s IPv4 TCP networking stack could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to trigger memory corruption, crash vulnerable systems, and potentially execute arbitrary code with root privileges. Tracked as CVE-2026-98432, the flaw carries a CVSS 3.1 score of 9.8 and has existed in the Linux kernel since version 4.4. The vulnerability stems from a race condition that can cause the kernel to access IP option data after the underlying memory has already been freed. An attacker capable of reaching an exposed IPv4 TCP service can attempt to trigger the condition using specially timed connection requests containing IPv4 options. No authentication, local privileges, or user interaction are required. Security interest increased significantly after Anthropic disclosed that an internal Claude research model had developed a working exploit capable of achieving remote root command execution against a Linux server with a Multipath TCP (MPTCP) listener. The exploit first leaks a kernel pointer to bypass KASLR and then uses the same use-after-free condition to corrupt memory and redirect kernel control flow. Anthropic has not released the exploit code. Importantly, the underlying vulnerability is not limited to MPTCP. Red Hat confirms that systems with ordinary IPv4 TCP networking remain vulnerable even when MPTCP is disabled, including default Red Hat Enterprise Linux configurations.
